newsitem.title: USA: CBOE says may halt trading in Centennial options.
newsitem.headline: CBOE says may halt trading in Centennial options.

text.p: The Chicago Board Options Exchange said Friday it will halt trading in options on Centennial Technologies Inc if the New York Stock Exchange suspends the stock and it fails to trade on another national exchange or the Nasdaq market on Monday, March 3.
The NYSE has said it intends to suspend Centennial shares prior to the opening on March 3 and will thereafter apply to federal regulators to delist them.
The CBOE said it would assess "on an ongoing basis" what type of trading restrictions on Centennial options should be in place if the stock is suspended for an extended period.
At the CBOE, Centennial options trading is restricted to closing transactions but no determination has been made to restrict exercises in the options, it said.
Centennial options trade on the CBOE and the American Stock Exchange.

Centennial shares lost three-quarters of their value on Thursday, falling 11-1/4 to 3-1/2, after the company said it would restate its earnings to show a loss for the last 3-1/2 years rather than a profit.
The shares were down a further 5/8 Friday afternoon at 2-7/8.
